subject.title: [Feature]: Plugin hot-reload without container restart (jiti cache invalidation)

question: Should OpenClaw support in-process reload of plugin code, or keep plugin source process-stable and limit the product to managed Gateway restart plus clearer diagnostics?
rationale: Both directions are technically viable, but in-process reload creates a durable plugin lifecycle and compatibility contract across many registration surfaces; automation cannot choose that product boundary safely.

options.title: Design transactional plugin reload
options.body: Add an explicit lifecycle and disposal contract plus an atomic Gateway reload operation before exposing a CLI command.

options.title: Keep restart-only semantics
options.body: Preserve process-stable plugin code, improve restart automation and log wording, and clearly document the supported development loop.

options.title: Expose cache clearing only
options.body: Add a cache command without runtime replacement, accepting that users must still restart and internal cache details become public surface.

recommendation.title: Design transactional plugin reload
recommendation.body: Add an explicit lifecycle and disposal contract plus an atomic Gateway reload operation before exposing a CLI command.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent history is in the central loader, Jiti cache, and reload-planning surfaces that define the feasible product boundary.
